paragraphs: I am May, and I love classical music. In my opinion, it is awesome because every instrument tells a part of a story. At home, my grandma listens to it in the evening, and my green parrot, Bill, sings with it. I do not play an instrument yet, but I want to learn the violin. Not everybody likes it, but I do.

On Monday, I saw an ad on the board in the school hall. It was very attractive, with a big red and gold violin in the middle. The words said, "SCHOOL CONCERT, FRIDAY, FOUR O'CLOCK, IN THE HALL." On the ad, a band of older students and a few musicians from the town stood on a stage. My brother Pat saw the ad too. "Are there drums?" he asked. "Yes, there is a big drum," I said.

At the club on Thursday, Leo looked at the ad on my tablet. "The ad is nice," he said, "but classical music is slow and boring." "Only a few children will come," he said. Among my friends, Leo is the one who says what he thinks, and I like that. "You do not know it," I said. "Listen for one minute, and then tell me."

Leo took a seat at the end of the table, far from me. Teacher Kim gave me the library speaker, and I played a fast piece. It began with a drum, and then the violins came in. Leo crossed his arms and looked at the ceiling. After twenty seconds, his foot began to move. Mia moved her head, and Lily closed her eyes. "This one is probably a fast one," said Leo. "Yes," I said. "It is about a storm at sea."

When the music stopped, nobody said a word. "Can we hear it again?" asked Mia. I played the piece again, and this time Leo closed his eyes. Then Leo said, "OK, it is not boring." "It is a story with no words." I did not tell him that sentence, because he found it himself. I thought of Pat and the big drum, and I smiled. Leo asked, "Can I come on Friday?" "Of course," I said. Before I went home, I wrote a small card and put it under the ad. It said, "Classical music is awesome. Come and listen!"
text.summary: May loves classical music and tells her opinion. She sees an ad for a school concert, Leo says the music is boring, and May plays him a fast piece until he changes his mind.
